chunks: And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Bint Ilyās, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj and Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān together, from Zurārah and Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

It is obligatory for the mustahadah to consider some of her womenfolk and follow their menstrual periods, then to add one day by way of precaution to that. This does not conflict with the earlier reports, because this is the ruling for one who has womenfolk; but as for one who has no womenfolk, or they differ, then the ruling is what we have mentioned. For that reason he said at the end of the report: if her womenfolk differ, then the maximum of her waiting is ten days and the minimum of it is three, so her ruling in that case is referred back to what the earlier reports contained.

key_terms.أَقْرَائِهَا: her menstrual periods or cycles used as a basis of comparison
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارَ الْأُولَى: the earlier hadith reports previously cited on this ruling
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةِ: a woman experiencing istiḥāḍah, irregular non-menstrual bleeding
key_terms.تَسْتَظْهِرَ: to add a precautionary period beyond the estimated days
key_terms.جُلُوسِهَا: her period of refraining, meaning the days treated as menstruation
key_terms.مُخْتَلِفَاتٍ: differing from one another in their menstrual patterns

ai.seo_question: How should a mustahadah determine her menstrual period if her bleeding continues and she has no fixed habit?
ai.summary: This report discusses the legal ruling for a woman experiencing istiḥāḍah when determining her menstrual period for ritual purposes. It explains that she should refer to the habitual cycles of related women and add a precautionary day, while if no such comparable women are available or they differ, the ruling returns to the earlier established reports.
